discoveries.text: QZS-1R belongs to Japan’s Michibiki navigation system, which works alongside GPS. In this recorded sky, it is 83° up, almost directly overhead.
This is Proba-3’s Occulter spacecraft, designed to block the Sun for its partner and create an artificial eclipse. That lets the other spacecraft study the Sun’s faint outer atmosphere.
THEMIS A is part of NASA’s mission investigating what triggers the northern and southern lights. In this snapshot, it is about 77,800 km from Seoul.
This satellite is only about 484 km from Seoul in this snapshot. Its calculated height above Earth is 470 km.
It is moving at 7.70 km/s in this snapshot—about 27,700 km/h.
Its orbit is strongly stretched, with eccentricity 0.84; a circle has eccentricity zero. Its distance from Earth changes greatly through each orbit.
Its orbit is tilted 89.0° to Earth’s equator—almost perpendicular. In this snapshot, it is 1,071 km above Earth.
One orbit takes about 23 hours 56 minutes, based on its orbital data—nearly a full day. Its calculated altitude here is 35,791 km.
One circuit of Earth takes about 92 minutes, based on its orbital data. That is roughly 16 orbits a day.
